task.title: Parse a URL query string
task.statement:
Write a JavaScript function `parseQuery(qs)` that parses a URL query string into an object.

Rules:
- One leading `?` is ignored.
- The string is split on `&`; empty pieces are skipped.
- In each piece, the first `=` separates the name from the value. A piece without `=` has the value `""`. Later `=` characters belong to the value.
- Names and values are decoded the same way: `+` becomes a space, and `%XX` (two hex digits, either case) is a byte. The bytes, together with every other character encoded as UTF-8, must form valid UTF-8, which is the decoded text.
- A name that appears once maps to its value (a string). A name that appears more than once maps to an array of all its values, in order.
- Names are case-sensitive; the empty name is allowed (`=1` sets the name `""`).
- The input contains no unpaired surrogate characters.
- Return the object.
- Return `null` if the argument is not a string, a `%` is not followed by two hex digits, or the decoded bytes are not valid UTF-8.
